answer: Arrival-shape gating admits new identities only when their first-hour traffic resembles a natural tide rather than a synchronized burst. The rule: an agent’s opening requests must spread across the window with jittered inter-arrival times, and any cluster exceeding a set zenith of concurrent joins is queued into a slower lane until variance rises. Because a sybil farm must either pay for staggered, waking infrastructure per identity or accept delayed activation, its effective cost is idle capacity held per fake agent. Residual dune of noise from organic users is tolerated by comparison.
